[LLM] n8n workflow API request body containing JS prototype pollution tokens (CVE-2026-44789) Exploitation High
Hunts for HTTP requests to the n8n workflow/execution API whose body or query string contains JavaScript prototype-pollution sentinels (`__proto__`, `constructor.prototype`, `__defineGetter__`) targeting the HTTP Request node pagination parameter. This is the article-specific pre-exploit signal for CVE-2026-44789. Rationale: Pivots on the exact prototype-pollution sentinels (`__proto__`, `constructor.prototype`, `__defineGetter__`) named in CWE-1321 / GHSA-c8xv-5998-g76h, scoped to the n8n REST/webhook URL surface where the pagination parameter is parsed. Cross-checked against GitHub GHSA advisory, Endor Labs write-up, and Cybersecurity News reporting. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c8xv-5998-g76h • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-44789 • https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/ • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1321.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let PollutionTokens = dynamic(["__proto__", "constructor.prototype", "__defineGetter__", "prototype[", "%5F%5Fproto%5F%5F", "%5Fproto%5F"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RemotePort in (5678, 443, 80) or LocalPort in (5678, 443, 80)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("node.exe", "n8n.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "n8n"
| where RemoteUrl has_any (PollutionTokens)
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (PollutionTokens)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, LocalPort, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let PollutionTokens = dynamic(["__proto__", "constructor.prototype", "__defineGetter__", "prototype[", "%5F%5Fproto%5F%5F", "%5Fproto%5F"]);
let IISHits = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where csUriStem has_any ("/rest/workflows", "/rest/executions", "/webhook")
    | where csUriQuery has_any (PollutionTokens) or csUriStem has_any (PollutionTokens)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, ClientIP = cIP, User = csUserName,
              Method = csMethod, Uri = csUriStem, Query = csUriQuery, UA = csUserAgent,
              Source = "W3CIISLog";
let CSLHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where RequestURL has_any ("/rest/workflows", "/rest/executions", "/webhook")
    | where RequestURL has_any (PollutionTokens) or Message has_any (PollutionTokens)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = DestinationHostName, ClientIP = SourceIP,
              User = SourceUserName, Method = RequestMethod, Uri = RequestURL,
              Query = RequestContext, UA = RequestClientApplication,
              Source = "CommonSecurityLog";
let WebHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where Url has_any ("/rest/workflows", "/rest/executions", "/webhook")
    | where Url has_any (PollutionTokens) or UrlOriginal has_any (PollutionTokens)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, ClientIP = SrcIpAddr,
              User = SrcUsername, Method = HttpMethod, Uri = Url,
              Query = UrlOriginal, UA = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent,
              Source = "ImWebSession";
union isfuzzy=true IISHits, CSLHits, WebHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects HTTP requests to n8n workflow/execution/webhook API endpoints whose URI or query string carries JavaScript prototype-pollution sentinel tokens used to exploit CVE-2026-44789 in the HTTP Request node pagination handler.
references:

logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_uri:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/rest/workflows'
      - '/rest/executions'
      - '/webhook'
  selection_payload:
    cs-uri-query|contains:
      - '__proto__'
      - 'constructor.prototype'
      - '__defineGetter__'
      - 'prototype['
      - '%5F%5Fproto%5F%5F'

falsepositives:
  - JavaScript prototype-pollution scanners (Burp, Acunetix, Nessus) run by internal security teams

[LLM] Post-exploit RCE: node.js (n8n) spawning shell or scripting interpreter Installation High
Detects the post-exploitation tail of CVE-2026-44789 — the n8n `node` process spawning a shell (`cmd.exe`, `sh`, `bash`, `powershell.exe`) or a LOLBin. Prototype-pollution RCEs land here because the polluted global lets the attacker reroute child-process spawning into arbitrary commands run as the n8n service account. Rationale: Uses the most reliable post-exploit signal — n8n's `node` process spawning a shell or LOLBin — which is the actual outcome chain described in GHSA-c8xv-5998-g76h ("combined with other techniques this could lead to RCE"). Article + Endor Labs corroboration both flag RCE as the impact, and CWE-1321 prototype-pollution chains universally land via hijacked child-process spawn. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c8xv-5998-g76h • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-44789 • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1321.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1059 T1059.001 T1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let ShellsAndLolbins = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","zsh","dash","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","nc","ncat","socat"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("n8n", "\\n8n\\", "/n8n/")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("n8n", "\\.n8n\\")
| where FileName in~ (ShellsAndLolbins)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let ShellsAndLolbins = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","zsh","dash","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","nc","ncat","socat"]);
let WinHits = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node\\","\\node")
    | where tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]) in~ (ShellsAndLolbins)
    | where (CommandLine has_any ("n8n")) or (ParentProcessName has "n8n") or true
    | where TargetUserName !endswith "$"
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, User=TargetUserName,
              ParentImage=ParentProcessName, ChildImage=NewProcessName,
              ChildCmd=CommandLine, Source="SecurityEvent";
let AsimHits = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node")
    | where ActingProcessName has_any (ShellsAndLolbins) or TargetProcessName has_any (ShellsAndLolbins)
    | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, User=ActorUsername,
              ParentImage=ParentProcessName, ChildImage=coalesce(TargetProcessName, ActingProcessName),
              ChildCmd=coalesce(TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessCommandLine),
              Source="ImProcessCreate";
union isfuzzy=true WinHits, AsimHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Vulnerable n8n versions in TVM inventory (CVE-2026-44789) Reconnaissance High
Surfaces hosts and software packages where n8n is installed at a version inside the CVE-2026-44789 vulnerable range (<1.123.43, 2.0.0-rc.0–2.20.6, 2.21.0–2.22.0). Pre-exploit asset visibility — without this UC the SOC is hunting blind for an attack surface they don't know they own. Rationale: Article explicitly enumerates vulnerable version ranges (npm:n8n <1.123.43; 2.0.0-rc.0–<2.20.7; 2.21.0–<2.22.1) — version-range matching against TVM inventory is the lowest-FP detection possible and the most operationally valuable pre-attack signal. Corroborated against the NVD CVE entry and the published patched versions. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c8xv-5998-g76h • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-44789
ATT&CKT1592.002 T1190
Data sources
DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
| where SoftwareName =~ "n8n" or SoftwareName has "n8n"
| extend Parts = split(SoftwareVersion, ".")
| extend Major = toint(Parts[0]), Minor = toint(Parts[1]), Patch = toint(Parts[2])
| extend Vulnerable = case(
    Major == 1 and (Minor < 123 or (Minor == 123 and Patch < 43)), "yes-1.x (<1.123.43)",
    Major == 2 and Minor >= 0 and Minor <= 19, strcat("yes-2.", tostring(Minor), " (<2.20.7)"),
    Major == 2 and Minor == 20 and Patch < 7, "yes-2.20.<7",
    Major == 2 and Minor == 21, "yes-2.21 (<2.22.1)",
    Major == 2 and Minor == 22 and Patch < 1, "yes-2.22.0",
    "no")
| where Vulnerable != "no"
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by DeviceId | project DeviceId, IsInternetFacing, OSPlatform) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, DeviceId, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, Vulnerable, IsInternetFacing, OSPlatform
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, DeviceName asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where CveId =~ "CVE-2026-44789" or SoftwareName has "n8n"
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by DeviceId, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by DeviceId | project DeviceId, IsInternetFacing, OSPlatform) on DeviceId
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, DeviceId, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion,
          CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, IsInternetFacing, OSPlatform
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, DeviceName asc

// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-44789")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-44789")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

[LLM] Inbound exploit attempt to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager from known UAT-8616 / Cluster IPs Exploitation High
Detects network connections from the Talos-published exploit-source IPs targeting Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager / vSmart (vManage) management interfaces. Anchors on the specific source IPs Talos attributes to UAT-8616 and Clusters 1-4 exploiting CVE-2026-20182 and the CVE-2026-20133/20128/20122 chain. Rationale: Source IPs are explicitly attributed by Talos to UAT-8616 (CVE-2026-20182) and Clusters 1-4 (CVE-2026-20133/20128/20122). Ports cover vManage HTTPS (443/8443), NETCONF (830), SD-WAN device control (4566), and SSH (22). Cross-checked with Cisco PSIRT advisory cisco-sa-sdwan-auth-bypass and Rapid7's disclosure referenced in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/publicationListing.x • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/sd-wan-ongoing-exploitation/

[LLM] XenShell / Godzilla / Behinder JSP webshell file write on Cisco SD-WAN Manager Installation High
Detects creation of the specific JSP webshell filenames Talos observed dropped on compromised Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager nodes after exploitation of CVE-2026-20133/20128/20122. Filenames are non-generic and attacker-chosen (20251117022131.jsp, conf.jsp, sysv.jsp, sysinit.jsp, vmurnp_ikp.jsp). Rationale: Filenames 20251117022131.jsp, conf.jsp, sysv.jsp, sysinit.jsp, vmurnp_ikp.jsp are explicitly named by Talos as attacker-dropped XenShell/Godzilla/Behinder variants on the SD-WAN Manager. Generic .jsp creation under vManage webapps directories also catches XenShell variants with rotating names since SD-WAN Manager should not be receiving developer-dropped JSPs in production. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/sd-wan-ongoing-exploitation/ • https://github.com/BeichenDream/Godzilla
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190

DeviceFileEvents

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc

imFileEvent

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] AdaptixC2 'shadowcore' / Mythic C2 traffic to UAT-8616 infrastructure 194.163.175.135 Command & Control High
Detects outbound traffic to the AdaptixC2/Mythic infrastructure Talos attributes to UAT-8616 — IP 194.163.175.135 hosting AdaptixC2 on port 4445 (banner renamed from 'AdapticC2 server' to 'shadowcore'), another AdaptixC2 listener on 31337, and a Mythic C2 listener on 7443 with certificate serial fece5b954e69b2c6a8d0a1029631a0d7. Rationale: 194.163.175.135 plus the trio of ports (4445 AdaptixC2 with 'shadowcore' banner, 7443 Mythic, 31337 second AdaptixC2 listener) and the Mythic cert serial fece5b954e69b2c6a8d0a1029631a0d7 are explicitly published by Talos as UAT-8616 infrastructure on Contabo GmbH. The IP-and-port tuple is high-fidelity because legitimate enterprise traffic to a Contabo VPS on these obscure ports is exceedingly rare. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/sd-wan-ongoing-exploitation/ • https://github.com/Adaptix-Framework/AdaptixC2 • https://github.com/its-a-feature/Mythic
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1573.002 T1095

| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] AdaptixC2 'systemd-resolved' or Sliver 'CWan' implant on Linux / SD-WAN host Installation High
Detects the specific implant filenames Talos observed dropped post-exploitation on Cisco SD-WAN devices: 'systemd-resolved' (AdaptixC2 agent masquerading as the legitimate Linux service) calling 194.163.175.135:4445, and 'CWan' (Sliver implant) calling mtls://23.27.143.170:443. Hunts both the file presence and the C2 callouts. Rationale: Talos explicitly names the implant filenames ('systemd-resolved' for AdaptixC2 and 'CWan' for Sliver) and the C2 endpoints (194.163.175.135:4445, mtls://23.27.143.170:443). The masquerade check excludes the legitimate /lib/systemd path for systemd-resolved, so any other path equals a high-fidelity hit. Verified Sliver and AdaptixC2 framework attribution via the public AdaptixC2 and Sliver project pages. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/sd-wan-ongoing-exploitation/ • https://github.com/BishopFox/sliver • https://github.com/Adaptix-Framework/AdaptixC2
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1059.004 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let C2_IPs = dynamic(["194.163.175.135","23.27.143.170"]);
let ImpostorPaths = dynamic(["/lib/systemd/systemd-resolved","/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-resolved","/usr/libexec/systemd/systemd-resolved"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
  | where (FileName =~ "systemd-resolved" and FolderPath !in~ (ImpostorPaths))
     or FileName =~ "CWan"
     or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("194.163.175.135","23.27.143.170")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AccountName),
(DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
  | where RemoteIP in (C2_IPs)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName)
| order by Timestamp desc
let C2_IPs = dynamic(["194.163.175.135","23.27.143.170"]);
let KeywordList = dynamic(["systemd-resolved","CWan","194.163.175.135","23.27.143.170","mtls://23.27.143.170"]);
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any (KeywordList)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, Facility, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects execution of attacker-dropped Linux implants observed by Cisco Talos on compromised Cisco SD-WAN devices — AdaptixC2 binary named 'systemd-resolved' calling 194.163.175.135 and Sliver binary 'CWan' calling 23.27.143.170.

[LLM] UAT-8616 post-compromise on SD-WAN: SSH key add, NETCONF edit, su root, XMRig miner.sh Actions on Objectives High
Detects the specific post-compromise actions Talos lists for UAT-8616 after exploitation of CVE-2026-20182/20127 — adding SSH keys, modifying NETCONF configuration, privilege escalation via 'su root -c id', plus Cluster 7's XMRig deployment via /tmp/moneroocean/miner.sh with config_background.json. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article's verbatim strings: Code Block 2 (/tmp/moneroocean/miner.sh --config=/tmp/moneroocean/config_background.json), Code Block 3 (su root -c id), and the named post-compromise actions Talos lists for UAT-8616 (SSH key addition, NETCONF configuration modification). The 'su root -c id' command is a UAT-8616 fingerprint — a sophisticated actor verifying root context after privilege escalation, not normal admin usage. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/sd-wan-ongoing-exploitation/ • https://moneroocean.stream/
ATT&CKT1098.004 T1543 T1548.003 T1496
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "su root" and ProcessCommandLine has "-c" and ProcessCommandLine has "id")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/tmp/moneroocean/miner.sh","config_background.json","moneroocean")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "authorized_keys" and FileName in~ ("bash","sh","tee","echo","cat","dd","cp"))
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "edit-config" and ProcessCommandLine has "netconf")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let Keywords = dynamic(["su root -c id","su root \u2013c id","/tmp/moneroocean/miner.sh","config_background.json","moneroocean","authorized_keys","edit-config","netconf"]);
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any (Keywords)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, Facility, SeverityLevel, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)

[LLM] FlowiseAI POST /api/v1/node-custom-function with NodeVM Sandbox-Escape Payload (CVE-2026-46442) Exploitation High
Hunts authenticated POST requests to the unprotected Flowise custom-function endpoint that carry the specific NodeVM-escape payload markers documented in CVE-2026-46442 (constructor.constructor, getBuiltinModule, child_process, execSync, error.name=Object.create). High fidelity because the URL is article-specific and the payload tokens are the exact escape primitive. Rationale: Three article-specific anchors: the exact endpoint path /api/v1/node-custom-function, the JSON body field name javascriptFunction, and the documented escape primitive (constructor.constructor / getBuiltinModule / child_process). The URL is unique to Flowise; the body markers are the exact NodeVM-escape technique cited in the GHSA. Cross-checked against the @flowiseai/nodevm fork and prior vm2 sandbox-escape literature (Semgrep, BleepingComputer). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9rvc-vf7m-pgm2 • https://github.com/FlowiseAI/nodevm • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/calling-back-to-vm2-and-escaping-sandbox/ • https://www.npmjs.com/package/@flowiseai/nodevm
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007 T1068
Data sourcesWeb
// IIS / App Service in front of Flowise (URL pivot — most reverse proxies don't log POST body)
let ProxyHits =
    W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where csMethod =~ "POST"
    | where csUriStem has "/api/v1/node-custom-function"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, cIP, csUserName, csUserAgent, scStatus, sPort;
// WAF / proxy that DOES log body or the request URL with payload markers
let WafHits =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
    | where RequestURL has "/api/v1/node-custom-function"
       or Message has_any ("constructor.constructor", "getBuiltinModule", "javascriptFunction", "child_process")
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourceUserName, RequestMethod, RequestURL, Message, DeviceAction;
union isfuzzy=true ProxyHits, WafHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Flowise node.exe Spawning OS Shell or Command-Line Utility - Post-Exploit RCE (CVE-2026-46442) Exploitation High
Detects the Flowise Node.js host process spawning a child shell or built-in OS utility (cmd, powershell, sh, bash, wmic, whoami, id, hostname, ipconfig) - the exact post-conditions of the documented NodeVM escape that calls child_process.execSync. The PoC literally runs 'id' as the validation payload. Rationale: The PoC in the advisory ends with cp.execSync('id') - guaranteeing node.exe forks a shell/utility. Parent=node.exe + parent-cmd contains flowise/packages/server + child=shell-or-recon is a combination that should never occur during normal Flowise operation; the application is a JS chatflow engine, not a process orchestrator. Pivot is high-fidelity because the parent context is article-specific. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9rvc-vf7m-pgm2 • https://github.com/FlowiseAI/nodevm • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/calling-back-to-vm2-and-escaping-sandbox/
ATT&CKT1059 T1059.003 T1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "node")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("flowise", "packages/server", "packages\\server", "@flowiseai")
     or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("flowise", "Flowise", "@flowiseai")
| where FileName in~ (
    "cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
    "wmic.exe","whoami.exe","hostname.exe","ipconfig.exe","net.exe",
    "net1.exe","netstat.exe","tasklist.exe","systeminfo.exe","reg.exe",
    "sh","bash","dash","zsh","id","uname","ifconfig","ip","ps",
    "curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat"
  )
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath,
          ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// Windows 4688 view
let WinHits =
    SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where ParentProcessName endswith "\\node.exe"
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("flowise", "Flowise", "@flowiseai", "packages\\server")
         or CommandLine has_any ("flowise", "Flowise")
    | where NewProcessName has_any (
        "\\cmd.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe",
        "\\wmic.exe","\\whoami.exe","\\hostname.exe","\\ipconfig.exe","\\net.exe",
        "\\reg.exe","\\tasklist.exe","\\systeminfo.exe","\\curl.exe")
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
              ParentProcessName, SubjectUserName;
// Linux / ASIM view
let LinuxHits =
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ParentProcessName endswith "/node" or ParentProcessName == "node"
    | where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("flowise", "packages/server", "@flowiseai")
    | where TargetProcessName endswith_cs "/sh"
         or TargetProcessName endswith_cs "/bash"
         or TargetProcessName endswith_cs "/dash"
         or TargetProcessName endswith_cs "/zsh"
         or TargetProcessName in ("id","uname","whoami","hostname","ifconfig","ip","ps","curl","wget","nc","ncat")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
              TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine,
              ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine;
union isfuzzy=true WinHits, LinuxHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Strapi CVE-2026-27886 exploit — `where[admin-relation][private-field]` query parameter against public Content API Exploitation High
Detects HTTP requests that abuse Strapi's relational filtering bug (CVE-2026-27886) by traversing `updatedBy`/`createdBy`/`publishedBy` joins into the `admin_users` table to read private fields such as `resetPasswordToken`, `email`, or `password`. The query parameter shape is unique to this vulnerability and rarely produced by legitimate clients. Rationale: Uses the exact malicious query-parameter regex published in the GHSA advisory (`where[updatedBy|createdBy|publishedBy][resetPasswordToken|password|email|...][$startsWith|...]=`). This shape is unique to the CVE-2026-27886 exploit chain — legitimate Strapi clients filter by content-type fields, never by admin-relation private fields. corroborated_sources field references the GHSA primary source. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rjg2-95x7-8qmx
ATT&CKT1190 T1212
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let LookbackHours = 24h;
let StrapiExploitRegex = @"(?i)where\[(updatedBy|createdBy|publishedBy)\]\[(email|password|resetPasswordToken|confirmationToken|firstname|lastname|preferedLanguage)\]\[\$(startsWith|contains|eq|gt|lt|ge|le|in|notIn|notNull|null)\]=";
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImWebSession
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
   | where Url matches regex StrapiExploitRegex
   | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, HttpHostName, HttpMethod, Url, HttpStatusCode, UA = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, Src = "ImWebSession"),
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
   | where csUriQuery matches regex StrapiExploitRegex
   | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr = cIP, HttpHostName = sSiteName, HttpMethod = csMethod, Url = strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery), HttpStatusCode = tostring(scStatus), UA = csUserAgent, Src = "W3CIISLog"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
   | where RequestURL matches regex StrapiExploitRegex
   | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr = SourceIP, HttpHostName = DestinationHostName, HttpMethod = RequestMethod, Url = RequestURL, HttpStatusCode = tostring(EventOutcome), UA = RequestClientApplication, Src = "CommonSecurityLog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Strapi CVE-2026-27886 Relational Filter Boolean-Oracle Exploit
id: 8a3c8e9d-7b5f-4c2a-9e1d-6f4b2c5a8e1f
status: experimental
description: Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-27886 in Strapi <5.37.0 via the `where[admin-relation][private-field][$op]=` query parameter on publicly-accessible Content API endpoints. Used to oracle-extract admin reset tokens from the admin_users table.
references:

  - attack.credential_access

  category: webserver
detection:

[LLM] Strapi boolean-oracle hex-alphabet brute force from single source Exploitation High
Detects the high-volume single-source brute-force pattern characteristic of CVE-2026-27886 oracle extraction: the same Content API endpoint hit dozens-to-hundreds of times from one IP with identical-shape `where[adminRel][field][$op]=<hex>` query strings where only the trailing filter value varies across the hex alphabet (`0`–`f`). Threshold-and-cardinality detection. Rationale: The article's IoC list explicitly calls out: 'High volume of public Content API requests from a single IP iterating through a hex alphabet (0-9, a-f) on the same content-type endpoint with progressively-longer filter values' and 'Sustained burst of identical-shape requests with only the trailing character of the filter value varying'. The detection codifies that — high request count + ≥16 distinct hex filter values + tight time window — into a threshold trigger. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rjg2-95x7-8qmx
ATT&CKT1212 T1190 T1110.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let LookbackHours = 6h;
let MinRequestsPerSource = 50;
let MinDistinctFilterValues = 16;  // hex alphabet width: 0-9,a-f
let MaxDurationSec = 1800;          // burst must be tight (~30 min) to count as oracle
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)where\[(updatedBy|createdBy|publishedBy)\]\[(email|password|resetPasswordToken|confirmationToken|firstname|lastname|preferedLanguage)\]\[\$"
| extend FilterValue = extract(@"(?i)where\[\w+\]\[\w+\]\[\$\w+\]=([0-9a-fA-F]+)", 1, Url)
| extend FilterFieldTuple = extract(@"(?i)(where\[\w+\]\[\w+\]\[\$\w+\])=", 1, Url)
| where isnotempty(FilterValue)
| summarize
    RequestCount   = count(),
    DistinctValues = dcount(FilterValue),
    SampleValues   = make_set(FilterValue, 20),
    DistinctTuples = dcount(FilterFieldTuple),
    SampleTuples   = make_set(FilterFieldTuple, 5),
    UAs            = make_set(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, 5),
    FirstSeen      = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen       = max(TimeGenerated)
    by SrcIpAddr, HttpHostName
| extend DurationSec = datetime_diff('second', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| where RequestCount >= MinRequestsPerSource and DistinctValues >= MinDistinctFilterValues and DurationSec <= MaxDurationSec
| order by RequestCount desc
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:iis OR source:strapi OR source:nodejs) (@http.url_details.queryString:*where\[updatedBy\]* OR @http.url_details.queryString:*where\[createdBy\]* OR @http.url_details.queryString:*where\[publishedBy\]*) @http.url_details.queryString:*\$startsWith* OR @http.url_details.queryString:*\$contains* OR @http.url_details.queryString:*\$eq*
WEB

[LLM] Strapi CVE-2026-27886 admin takeover — exploit burst followed by `/admin/reset-password` POST Actions on Objectives High
Correlates a burst of CVE-2026-27886 oracle-extraction requests against a Strapi host with a subsequent `POST /admin/reset-password` call on the same host within 30 minutes. This is the closing move of the documented account-takeover chain: oracle-extract a reset token, then call the admin reset-password endpoint with it. Rationale: The article's IoC list specifies two final-stage signals: 'Subsequent POST /admin/reset-password calls using a reset token that the legitimate admin did not request' and 'Successful admin password change immediately following a burst of public Content API requests with where[updatedBy] query parameters'. The detection chains them at the per-host level with a 30-minute follow-on window — the same shape as the documented end-to-end takeover. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rjg2-95x7-8qmx
ATT&CKT1078 T1212 T1098
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let LookbackHours = 24h;
let ChainWindow   = 30min;
let MinExploitReqs = 10;
let StrapiExploitRegex = @"(?i)where\[(updatedBy|createdBy|publishedBy)\]\[(email|password|resetPasswordToken|confirmationToken|firstname|lastname|preferedLanguage)\]\[\$";
let ExploitBursts =
    ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
    | where Url matches regex StrapiExploitRegex
    | summarize ExploitCount = count(), FirstExploit = min(TimeGenerated), LastExploit = max(TimeGenerated), ExploitSrcIPs = make_set(SrcIpAddr, 10) by HttpHostName
    | where ExploitCount >= MinExploitReqs;
let ResetCalls =
    ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
    | where Url has "/admin/reset-password"
    | where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
    | project ResetTime = TimeGenerated, ResetHost = HttpHostName, ResetSrcIp = SrcIpAddr, ResetUrl = Url, ResetUA = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent;
ExploitBursts
| join kind=inner ResetCalls on $left.HttpHostName == $right.ResetHost
| where ResetTime between (FirstExploit .. (LastExploit + ChainWindow))
| extend ChainLatencySec = datetime_diff('second', ResetTime, LastExploit)
| project FirstExploit, LastExploit, ResetTime, ChainLatencySec, HttpHostName, ExploitCount, ExploitSrcIPs, ResetSrcIp, ResetUrl, ResetUA
| order by ResetTime desc

[LLM] Vulnerable Amazon Redshift JDBC Driver (CVE-2026-8178) inventory hunt — redshift-jdbc42 < 2.2.2 Reconnaissance High
Surfaces every host/asset where Defender TVM (or equivalent vuln scanner) reports the Amazon Redshift JDBC Driver below the patched 2.2.2 release, so the SOC can prioritise patching/segmentation of the JVMs whose classpath could be weaponised through CVE-2026-8178. Rationale: Pivots on the explicit CVE id and the affected Maven coordinate (`com.amazon.redshift:redshift-jdbc42` < 2.2.2) called out in the GHSA. Since the article confirms the fix landed in 2.2.2, the version-prefix exclusion list (2.2.2/.3/.4/.5/.6) is a precise inventory filter — false positives only when TVM lags on a freshly patched host. Joining DeviceInfo flags Internet-facing JVM hosts so the SOC can sequence patching by exposure. Datadog left blank because TVM CVE coverage is not shipped to Datadog logs in this estate; Sigma left blank because TVM is a snapshot, not an event-shaped log. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/aws/amazon-redshift-jdbc-driver/security/advisories/GHSA-wmmv-vvg5-993q • https://aws.amazon.com/security/security-bulletins/rss/2026-028-aws/ • https://radar.offseq.com/threat/cve-2026-8178-cwe-470-use-of-externally-controlled-c4285304 • https://github.com/aws/amazon-redshift-jdbc-driver/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md

[LLM] CVE-2026-8178 exploit attempt: Redshift JDBC URL with class-loading parameter (socketFactory/sslfactory/sslhostnameverifier/sslpasswordcallb Exploitation High
Hunts for the specific exploit primitive of CVE-2026-8178 — a `jdbc:redshift://` connection string carrying one of the four parameters (`socketFactory`, `sslfactory`, `sslhostnameverifier`, `sslpasswordcallback`) the unpatched driver instantiates without type-checking. Surfaces the URL whether it appears in a JVM command line, a connection-string env-var passed at fork, or a webapp HTTP request that accepts user-supplied JDBC URLs (DataEase-style sink). Rationale: The four parameter names (`socketFactory`, `sslfactory`, `sslhostnameverifier`, `sslpasswordcallback`) are the documented type-confusion sinks where the unpatched driver `Class.forName()`-then-instantiates whatever class name the JDBC URL specifies — confirmed by the AWS security bulletin and the related historical advisory chain (CVE-2022-41828, CVE-2024-12744). Pairing them with the `jdbc:redshift` scheme literal and the `java.exe`/`javaw.exe` image gives a 3-of-3 high-fidelity composite that has effectively zero benign use. The web-tier branch catches the DataEase-style sink where a webapp accepts user-supplied JDBC URLs (corroborated by GHSA-mfg2-qr5c-99pp). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/aws/amazon-redshift-jdbc-driver/security/advisories/GHSA-wmmv-vvg5-993q • https://aws.amazon.com/security/security-bulletins/rss/2026-028-aws/ • https://github.com/murataydemir/CVE-2022-41828 • https://github.com/dataease/dataease/security/advisories/GHSA-mfg2-qr5c-99pp • https://aws.amazon.com/security/security-bulletins/AWS-2024-015/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007 T1203

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("java.exe","javaw.exe") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe","javaw.exe")
| extend cmd = strcat(tolower(ProcessCommandLine), " || ", tolower(InitiatingProcessCommandLine))
| where cmd has_any (jdbc_pivot)
| where cmd has_any (vuln_params)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FileName,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-8178 — Redshift JDBC URL with class-loading params (process + web tier)
let vuln_params = dynamic(["socketFactory=","sslfactory=","sslhostnameverifier=","sslpasswordcallback="]);
let jdbc_pivot  = dynamic(["jdbc:redshift","jdbc%3aredshift"]);
let ProcessHits =
    SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | extend NewProcLower = tolower(NewProcessName), CmdLower = tolower(CommandLine)
    | where NewProcLower endswith "\\java.exe" or NewProcLower endswith "\\javaw.exe"
    | where CmdLower has_any (jdbc_pivot)
    | where CmdLower has_any (vuln_params)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source = "Process";
let WebHits =
    W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | extend QueryLower = tolower(strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery))
    | where QueryLower has_any (jdbc_pivot)
    | where QueryLower has_any (vuln_params)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, Url = strcat(csUriStem,"?",csUriQuery), csUserAgent, scStatus, Source = "IIS";
union isfuzzy=true ProcessHits, WebHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Kimsuky targets organizations with PebbleDash-based tools
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Kimsuky HelloDoor 'tdll' Run-key persistence with regsvr32 loader · [LLM] Kimsuky httpMalice persistence: 'Everything 1.9a-/1.8a-' Run-key or CacheDB service install · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Kimsuky HelloDoor 'tdll' Run-key persistence with regsvr32 loader Installation High
Hunts the autorun footprint of HelloDoor, Kimsuky's first Rust-based PebbleDash variant. HelloDoor uniquely registers itself under HKCU\...\Run with the value name 'tdll' and a data string invoking 'regsvr32.exe /s [DLL path]'. The combination of that exact value name and a regsvr32 silent-load command in a Run key is article-specific and not seen in benign software. Rationale: The article explicitly names the Run-key value 'tdll' and data 'regsvr32.exe /s [current file path]' as HelloDoor's persistence routine. 'tdll' has no documented benign use and the regsvr32 silent flag adds further specificity. Token-aligned matches on the registry path and value data make this a tight, low-FP detection. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/kimsuky-appleseed-pebbledash-campaigns/119785/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0094/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1218.010
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has @"\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run"
| where RegistryValueName =~ "tdll"
| where RegistryValueData has "regsvr32" and RegistryValueData has "/s"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RegistryKey has @"\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run"
| where RegistryValue =~ "tdll"
| where RegistryValueData has "regsvr32" and RegistryValueData has "/s"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Kimsuky HelloDoor 'tdll' Run-Key Persistence with regsvr32 Loader

[LLM] Kimsuky httpMalice persistence: 'Everything 1.9a-/1.8a-' Run-key or CacheDB service install Installation High
Hunts httpMalice (latest PebbleDash backdoor variant) establishing persistence. Depending on token elevation, it either creates a service named 'CacheDB' (display name 'Administrator', running 'rundll32.exe [dll path], load') or writes an HKCU Run-key value named 'Everything 1.9a-[filesize]' (or older 'Everything 1.8a-[filesize]'). Both indicators are uniquely tied to httpMalice. Rationale: The article literally names 'Everything 1.9a-[filesize]' / 'Everything 1.8a-[filesize]' as the Run-key value names httpMalice writes, and 'CacheDB' (with 'rundll32.exe [DLL], load' image path and 'Administrator' display name) as the service it creates when elevated. Both strings are bespoke to httpMalice — joining registry + service-install telemetry captures both code paths. Sigma omitted because the rule is a union of two distinct event shapes (registry value set + service install). Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/kimsuky-appleseed-pebbledash-campaigns/119785/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0094/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003/
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1543.003 T1218.011
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Services
union
(DeviceRegistryEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
  | where RegistryKey has @"\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run"
  | where RegistryValueName matches regex @"(?i)^Everything 1\.[89]a-\d+$"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            Signal = "httpMalice RunKey (Everything 1.9a-/1.8a-)",
            Detail = strcat(RegistryValueName, " => ", RegistryValueData)),
(DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where ActionType == "ServiceInstalled"
  | extend AF = parse_json(AdditionalFields)
  | extend SvcName = tostring(AF.ServiceName), SvcImage = tostring(AF.ServiceFileName)
  | where SvcName =~ "CacheDB"
  | where SvcImage has "rundll32" and SvcImage has ",load"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            Signal = "httpMalice CacheDB service install",
            Detail = SvcImage)
| order by Timestamp desc
union
(ImRegistryEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RegistryKey has @"\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run"
  | where RegistryValue matches regex @"(?i)^Everything 1\.[89]a-\d+$"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
            Signal = "httpMalice RunKey (Everything 1.9a-/1.8a-)",
            Detail = strcat(RegistryValue, " => ", RegistryValueData)),
(Event
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where EventLog == "System" and EventID == 7045
  | where RenderedDescription has "CacheDB"
  | where RenderedDescription has "rundll32" and RenderedDescription has ",load"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname = Computer, ActorUsername = UserName, ActingProcessName = "services.exe",
            Signal = "httpMalice CacheDB service install",
            Detail = RenderedDescription)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 @TargetObject:(*\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\Everything\ 1.9a-* OR *\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\Everything\ 1.8a-* OR *\\currentversion\\run\\Everything\ 1.9a-* OR *\\currentversion\\run\\Everything\ 1.8a-*)) OR (source:windows.security @EventID:7045 @ServiceName:CacheDB @ImagePath:(*rundll32* OR *RunDll32* OR *RUNDLL32*))
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\CurrentVersion\\Run*" (Registry.registry_value_name="Everything 1.9a-*" OR Registry.registry_value_name="Everything 1.8a-*") by host Registry.user Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
| eval signal="httpMalice Run key (Everything 1.9a-/1.8a-)"
| append [
    | tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Services where Services.service_name="CacheDB" Services.service_path="*rundll32*,load*" by host Services.service_name Services.service_path Services.start_mode
    | `drop_dm_object_name(Services)`
    | eval signal="httpMalice CacheDB service install"
  ]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\CurrentVersion\\Run*" (Registry.registry_value_name="Everything 1.9a-*" OR Registry.registry_value_name="Everything 1.8a-*") by host Registry.user Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
| eval signal="httpMalice Run key (Everything 1.9a-/1.8a-)"
| append [
    | tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Services where Services.service_name="CacheDB" Services.service_path="*rundll32*,load*" by host Services.service_name Services.service_path Services.start_mode
    | `drop_dm_object_name(Services)`
    | eval signal="httpMalice CacheDB service install"
  ]
[LLM] Kimsuky JSE dropper: wscript -> powershell hidden + certutil -decode chain Delivery High
Hunts the literal command-line emitted by Kimsuky's JSE droppers (HelloDoor, httpMalice, AppleSeed deliveries): 'powershell.exe -windowstyle hidden certutil -decode [src] [dst]'. The dropper executes via wscript.exe (default JSE handler), shells PowerShell hidden, and uses certutil to base64-decode the second-stage payload before invoking it with regsvr32/rundll32. Rationale: Direct quote from the article: 'The malicious payload leverages powershell.exe -windowstyle hidden certutil -decode [src path] [dst path] for the second Base64 decoding before execution.' JSE files are handled by wscript.exe by default. The four-token combination (windowstyle + hidden + certutil + -decode in one cmdline, parented by a script host) is essentially never seen in benign software. Defender query also chains to the follow-on regsvr32/rundll32 from C:\ProgramData mentioned in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/kimsuky-appleseed-pebbledash-campaigns/119785/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0094/ • https://lolbas-project.github.io/lolbas/Binaries/Certutil/
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.005 T1140 T1564.003 T1218.010
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "powershell.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "windowstyle" and ProcessCommandLine has "hidden"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "certutil" and ProcessCommandLine has "-decode"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","explorer.exe","cmd.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName in~ ("regsvr32.exe","rundll32.exe")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "powershell.exe"
    | where FolderPath has @"C:\ProgramData" or ProcessCommandLine has @"C:\ProgramData"
    | project FollowOnTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, FollowOnCmd = ProcessCommandLine, FollowOnFile = FileName
  ) on DeviceName
| where isnull(FollowOnTime) or FollowOnTime between (Timestamp .. Timestamp + 5m)
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetProcessName endswith "powershell.exe"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "windowstyle" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "hidden"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "certutil" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "-decode"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","explorer.exe","cmd.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium

ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("995a0a49ae4b244928b3f67e2bfd7a6e", "52f1ff082e981cbdfd1f045c6021c63f", "65fc9f06de5603e2c1af9b4f288bb22c", "8e15c4d4f71bdd9dbc48cd2cabc87806", "8983ffa6da23e0b99ccc58c17b9788c7") or SHA1 in~ ("995a0a49ae4b244928b3f67e2bfd7a6e", "52f1ff082e981cbdfd1f045c6021c63f", "65fc9f06de5603e2c1af9b4f288bb22c", "8e15c4d4f71bdd9dbc48cd2cabc87806", "8983ffa6da23e0b99ccc58c17b9788c7") or MD5 in~ ("995a0a49ae4b244928b3f67e2bfd7a6e", "52f1ff082e981cbdfd1f045c6021c63f", "65fc9f06de5603e2c1af9b4f288bb22c", "8e15c4d4f71bdd9dbc48cd2cabc87806", "8983ffa6da23e0b99ccc58c17b9788c7")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("995a0a49ae4b244928b3f67e2bfd7a6e", "52f1ff082e981cbdfd1f045c6021c63f", "65fc9f06de5603e2c1af9b4f288bb22c", "8e15c4d4f71bdd9dbc48cd2cabc87806", "8983ffa6da23e0b99ccc58c17b9788c7") or SHA1 in~ ("995a0a49ae4b244928b3f67e2bfd7a6e", "52f1ff082e981cbdfd1f045c6021c63f", "65fc9f06de5603e2c1af9b4f288bb22c", "8e15c4d4f71bdd9dbc48cd2cabc87806", "8983ffa6da23e0b99ccc58c17b9788c7") or MD5 in~ ("995a0a49ae4b244928b3f67e2bfd7a6e", "52f1ff082e981cbdfd1f045c6021c63f", "65fc9f06de5603e2c1af9b4f288bb22c", "8e15c4d4f71bdd9dbc48cd2cabc87806", "8983ffa6da23e0b99ccc58c17b9788c7")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["995a0a49ae4b244928b3f67e2bfd7a6e", "52f1ff082e981cbdfd1f045c6021c63f", "65fc9f06de5603e2c1af9b4f288bb22c", "8e15c4d4f71bdd9dbc48cd2cabc87806", "8983ffa6da23e0b99ccc58c17b9788c7"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] FrostyNeighbor PicassoLoader drop to %AppData%\WinDataScope\Update.js Installation High
Hunts the article-specific second-stage drop: a JavaScript PicassoLoader payload written to a fixed AppData subfolder ('WinDataScope') used by FrostyNeighbor's March 2026 Ukrtelecom-themed compromise chain. The folder name and filename are both fingerprinted by ESET against multiple samples in this campaign. Rationale: WinDataScope is a folder name nowhere referenced in legitimate software inventories — ESET fingerprints it directly to FrostyNeighbor's PicassoLoader staging in the May 2026 report. Combined with the file name Update.js this is a near-zero-FP file-write signature. Cross-checked against: • https://cert.gov.ua/article/40240 • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1010/ • https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/
ATT&CKT1027.009 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has @"\AppData\Roaming\WinDataScope" and FileName =~ "Update.js"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA1, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType =~ "FileCreated" or EventType =~ "FileModified"
| where TargetFilePath has @"\AppData\Roaming\WinDataScope" and TargetFileName =~ "Update.js"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath,
          TargetFileSHA1, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: FrostyNeighbor PicassoLoader Drop to WinDataScope AppData Folder
id: 7d83e1b4-3c2f-4d09-9f56-0b1a4f6e02d1
description: Detects JavaScript file Update.js being written under %AppData%\Roaming\WinDataScope, the fixed staging path used by FrostyNeighbor (Ghostwriter/UNC1151) PicassoLoader in the March 2026 Ukrtelecom lure campaign documented by ESET.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/frostyneighbor-fresh-mischief-digital-shenanigans/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/19
tags:
  - attack.t1027.009
  - attack.t1036.005
  - attack.persistence
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains: '\AppData\Roaming\WinDataScope\'
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\Update.js'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - No known legitimate software uses this folder name
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:*\\WinDataScope\\Update.js OR @TargetFilename:*\\windatascope\\update.js OR @TargetFilename:*\\WINDATASCOPE\\UPDATE.JS)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\AppData\\Roaming\\WinDataScope\\Update\.js$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT

[LLM] FrostyNeighbor JS dropper self-relaunch with --update flag Exploitation High
Detects the FrostyNeighbor first-stage JavaScript dropper's documented self-relaunch pattern: wscript.exe / cscript.exe executes a .js file with the literal '--update' argument so the second branch of the script can install PicassoLoader. The flag string is bespoke to this campaign and is not used by legitimate Windows Script Host workflows. Rationale: The article explicitly states the first-stage script re-executes itself with the --update flag to branch into the PicassoLoader drop. The double-dash --update form is uncommon in WSH-launched JavaScript and pairs with a .js argument that is rarely seen in benign workflows. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/007/ • https://cert.gov.ua/article/40240
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--update"
| where ProcessCommandLine has ".js"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "--update" and ActingProcessCommandLine has ".js"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] FrostyNeighbor C2 callout to needbinding/nebao/algsat/sardk/alexavegas/lavanille Command & Control High
Detects DNS or HTTP egress to the six FrostyNeighbor C2 domains published by ESET in May 2026 (PicassoLoader on five .icu hosts plus a .buzz Cobalt Strike host). All six share the same actor infrastructure cluster registered between 2026-03-10 and 2026-04-14. Rationale: ESET published the full domain list in Table 2 of the article alongside first-seen dates from a freshly-registered actor infrastructure cluster (.icu/.buzz, no legitimate corporate use). Any host in a UA/PL/LT/EE government estate touching these domains is high-fidelity actor traffic. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1010/ • https://cert.gov.ua/article/40240
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1583.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
let FrostyDomains = dynamic(["needbinding.icu","nebao.icu","algsat.icu","alexavegas.icu","sardk.icu","lavanille.buzz"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (FrostyDomains)
    | extend Source="NetworkEvent"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source;
let EventHits = DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where ActionType =~ "DnsQueryResponse"
    | extend QueriedDomain = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).DnsQueryString)
    | where QueriedDomain has_any (FrostyDomains)
    | extend Source="DnsQuery"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP="", RemoteUrl=QueriedDomain,
              RemotePort=tolong(0),
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName, Source;
union NetHits, EventHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let FrostyDomains = dynamic(["needbinding.icu","nebao.icu","algsat.icu","alexavegas.icu","sardk.icu","lavanille.buzz"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (ImDnsActivity
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where DnsQuery has_any (FrostyDomains)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Domain=DnsQuery, Source="DNS"),
    (ImWebSession
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where Url has_any (FrostyDomains) or HttpHostName has_any (FrostyDomains)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Domain=coalesce(HttpHostName,Url), Source="HTTP"),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where RequestURL has_any (FrostyDomains) or DestinationHostName has_any (FrostyDomains)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=SourceHostName, SrcIpAddr=SourceIP, SrcUsername=SourceUserName, Domain=coalesce(DestinationHostName,RequestURL), Source="FW")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] PicassoLoader scheduled-task creation by wscript/cscript after C2 XML fetch Installation Medium
Detects FrostyNeighbor's persistence step: the JavaScript dropper downloads a scheduled-task XML template (served via the misleading Content-Type/Content-Disposition response to a .jpg URL) and then registers it. The parent-child chain of WSH spawning schtasks.exe or powershell.exe Register-ScheduledTask is article-specific. Rationale: The article describes the script downloading 'https://book-happy.needbinding[.]icu/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/1GreenAM.jpg' (which actually returns config.xml with Content-Type: application/xml) and then using it for persistence. Wscript/cscript spawning schtasks /Create /XML is a tight, low-FP pivot specific to this WSH-driven persistence pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/ • https://cert.gov.ua/article/40240
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where (FileName =~ "schtasks.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/Create","/XML"))
      or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "Register-ScheduledTask")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ChildProcess=FileName, ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcess=InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          GrandparentProcess=InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where (ActingProcessName has "schtasks.exe" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/Create","/XML"))
      or (ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ActingProcessCommandLine has "Register-ScheduledTask")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: WSH-Initiated Scheduled Task Registration (FrostyNeighbor PicassoLoader)
id: 2c8f47a3-9b14-4ee5-b87e-91a4f5d63c11
description: Detects wscript.exe or cscript.exe spawning schtasks.exe /Create /XML or powershell Register-ScheduledTask. This is the persistence step in FrostyNeighbor's March 2026 PicassoLoader chain, in which an XML template is downloaded under a fake .jpg URL and registered as a scheduled task.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/frostyneighbor-fresh-mischief-digital-shenanigans/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/19
tags:
  - attack.t1053.005
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.persistence
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  child_schtasks:
    Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/Create'
      - '/XML'
  child_pwsh:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'Register-ScheduledTask'
  condition: parent and (child_schtasks or child_pwsh)
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate vendor installers that use JScript wrappers to register tasks (rare)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\CScript.exe OR *\\WSCRIPT.EXE OR *\\CSCRIPT.EXE)) ((@Image:(*\\schtasks.exe OR *\\SchTasks.exe OR *\\SCHTASKS.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*/Create* OR */XML*)) OR (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe) AND @CommandLine:*Register-ScheduledTask*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i
| (ImageFileName=/schtasks\.exe$/i AND regex("(/Create|/XML)", field=CommandLine))
  OR (ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i AND regex("Register-ScheduledTask", field=CommandLine))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

[LLM] FrostyNeighbor Cobalt Strike beacon ViberPC.dll image load Installation High
Detects loading of ViberPC.dll, the final-stage Cobalt Strike beacon FrostyNeighbor masquerades as the legitimate Viber desktop messenger DLL. ESET publishes a SHA-1 (43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB) and the file is expected outside the legitimate Viber install path under the standard Cobalt Strike beacon naming pattern Win32/CobaltStrike.Beacon.S. Rationale: ESET published the exact SHA-1 (43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB) for the ViberPC.dll Cobalt Strike beacon in Table 1, classified Win32/CobaltStrike.Beacon.S. Combined with masquerading detection — ViberPC.dll loaded from a non-Viber path — this is a high-confidence final-stage beacon detection. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1010/ • https://cert.gov.ua/article/40240
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1055.001 T1588.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let FrostyHashes = dynamic(["43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB"]);
let ImageLoads = DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where FileName =~ "ViberPC.dll"
    | where SHA1 in~ (FrostyHashes)
         or not (FolderPath has @"\Viber\" or FolderPath has @"\Program Files\Viber")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source="ImageLoad";
let FileWrites = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where FileName =~ "ViberPC.dll"
    | where SHA1 in~ (FrostyHashes)
         or not (FolderPath has @"\Viber\" or FolderPath has @"\Program Files\Viber")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source="FileWrite";
union ImageLoads, FileWrites
| order by Timestamp desc
let FrostyHashes = dynamic(["43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "ViberPC.dll"
| where TargetFileSHA1 in~ (FrostyHashes)
     or not (TargetFilePath has @"\Viber\" or TargetFilePath has @"\Program Files\Viber")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath,
          TargetFileSHA1, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
