Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    from datamodel=Web

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB") or SHA1 in~ ("776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB") or MD5 in~ ("776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB") or SHA1 in~ ("776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB") or MD5 in~ ("776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-20182")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-20182")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

[LLM] Strapi Content-Type Builder Write API Reached in Production (CVE-2026-22599) Exploitation Medium
Detects POST/PUT to Strapi's Content-Type Builder write endpoint from a non-internal source. Per the patch (v5.33.2 / v4.26.1) these endpoints are disabled outside dev mode and return 404 — any successful POST/PUT in production indicates an unpatched instance under active exploitation or pre-patch admin misuse, both worth alerting on. Rationale: Anchored to the article's primary IOC — the literal endpoint path `/content-type-builder/content-types` and the (POST|PUT) verb regex. The patch behavior (404 in production) is what makes any such request high-signal: the article explicitly states the patch 'returns 404 for requests against /content-type-builder/content-types... removing the network-reachable attack surface entirely'. Splunk filters out RFC1918/loopback to focus on internet-reachable instances; Sentinel uses ImWebSession + not(ipv4_is_private) for the same effect. Defender Advanced Hunting has no native web access-log table, so defender_kql is empty (this telemetry lives in W3CIISLog / WAF logs, not DeviceProcessEvents).
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesWeb
// Strapi Content-Type Builder endpoint should return 404 in production (v5.33.2+/v4.26.1+)
// Any POST/PUT reaching it from a non-internal source = exploit attempt or unpatched instance
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where HttpMethod in ("POST","PUT")
| where Url contains "/content-type-builder/content-types"
| where isnotempty(SrcIpAddr)
| where not(ipv4_is_private(SrcIpAddr))
| where not(SrcIpAddr startswith "127.")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, HttpMethod, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpRequestHeaderReferer
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Strapi Content-Type Builder Write Followed by Server-Side Error (CVE-2026-22599 DoS / migration crash) Exploitation Medium
Detects POST/PUT to the Strapi Content-Type Builder content-types endpoint that returns a 5xx status — the article's explicit IOC for exploitation is 'Strapi server crashes immediately following a content-type creation or update, observed as the Node process exiting during the schema-migration step'. A 502/503/504 (upstream Strapi unreachable) or 500 from the Strapi node itself, gated to this specific URI, is a high-fidelity DoS / migration-error signal for the isRaw raw() injection. Rationale: Uses the article's explicit behavioural IOC — 'Strapi server crashes immediately following a content-type creation or update, observed as the Node process exiting during the schema-migration step'. A failed migration manifests as a 5xx on the same HTTP transaction (500 from Strapi itself, 502/503/504 from the upstream reverse proxy after node exits), so a single-event filter on (POST|PUT) + /content-type-builder/ + status≥500 is high-fidelity and Sigma-compatible. Datadog query left empty because the standard log sources listed (cloudtrail, azure.*, windows.*, linux.*, gcp.audit, kubernetes.audit, okta) do not include a generic web-access source — this telemetry would arrive at Datadog via a custom nginx/apache source not enumerated in the schema reference. Defender has no native web-access-log table.
ATT&CKT1190 T1499.004
Data sourcesWeb
// Schema-migration crash signature for CVE-2026-22599: 5xx response to a Content-Type Builder write
// Mirrors article IOC: 'Node process exiting during the schema-migration step'
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where HttpMethod in ("POST","PUT")
| where Url contains "/content-type-builder/"
| where HttpStatusCode between (500 .. 599)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, HttpMethod, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), DistinctUrls = make_set(Url, 25), Statuses = make_set(HttpStatusCode, 10) by SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, HttpMethod
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] SiYuan Electron renderer spawns shell/scripting child (CVE-2026-45375 Bazaar XSS → RCE) Exploitation High
Hunts the post-exploit RCE step of CVE-2026-45375. The SiYuan Bazaar XSS pivots to OS command execution via Node's child_process from a renderer with nodeIntegration=true. A SiYuan main/renderer process spawning cmd/powershell/pwsh/wscript/cscript/bash/sh/osascript/open/calc is highly anomalous — SiYuan is a markdown notes app and does not legitimately invoke shells. Rationale: Direct from the article: the renderer runs with `nodeIntegration:true`, `contextIsolation:false`, `webSecurity:false` (app/electron/main.js:407-411) and the Electron RCE PoC explicitly substitutes `require('child_process').exec('open -a Calculator')` as the payload string. Any shell/scripting child of siyuan.exe is therefore the executed payload. Cross-checked against memory observation 392 (SiYuan Electron RCE CVE cluster). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-27qc-m5gf-jv5r
ATT&CKT1059 T1203 T1189

[LLM] SiYuan Bazaar manifest written with embedded HTML/script markers (CVE-2026-45375 dropper) Delivery Medium
Hunts the dropper stage of CVE-2026-45375. A malicious Bazaar package's `plugin.json` / `theme.json` / `template.json` / `widget.json` / `icon.json` carrying HTML in the unsanitized `name` or `version` fields lands in the SiYuan workspace under `data/plugins/`, `data/themes/`, etc. Honest assumption: the file is dropped by something other than siyuan.exe itself (file-system sync, archive extraction, sideload) — siyuan.exe → manifest is the legitimate marketplace path. Targets the workspace manifest pattern named by the advisory. Rationale: Article names the exact five manifest filenames (plugin.json/theme.json/template.json/widget.json/icon.json), the exact workspace layout (`/tmp/siyuan-poc-ws/data/plugins/evil-plugin/plugin.json` in the Docker PoC), and the unescaped fields (`name`, `version`). FileSize > 2048 is a heuristic — clean manifests in the wild are ~200-600 bytes; the PoC payload bloats them. Tier=hunting because content inspection would be required to confirm the HTML payload — without it some baseline noise from legitimate marketplace installs is expected. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-27qc-m5gf-jv5r
ATT&CKT1546 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
// CVE-2026-45375 — SiYuan Bazaar manifest dropped in workspace (potential payload carrier)
let _manifest_names = dynamic(["plugin.json","theme.json","template.json","widget.json","icon.json"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName in~ (_manifest_names)
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\data\plugins\", @"\data\themes\", @"\data\templates\", @"\data\widgets\", @"\data\icons\",
                            "/data/plugins/", "/data/themes/", "/data/templates/", "/data/widgets/", "/data/icons/")
// honest manifests are tiny (~200-500 bytes); HTML/JS payload bloats them, OR a non-siyuan writer = sideload
| where FileSize > 2048
   or not(InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("siyuan.exe","siyuan"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, FileSize, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-45375 — Sentinel ASIM port
let _manifest_names = dynamic(["plugin.json","theme.json","template.json","widget.json","icon.json"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName in~ (_manifest_names)
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\data\plugins\", @"\data\themes\", @"\data\templates\", @"\data\widgets\", @"\data\icons\",
                                 "/data/plugins/","/data/themes/","/data/templates/","/data/widgets/","/data/icons/")
| where TargetFileSize > 2048
   or not(ActingProcessName has_any ("siyuan.exe","siyuan"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath,
          TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine

[LLM] Goobi viewer unauthenticated Solr streaming-expression proxy access (CVE-2026-45083) Exploitation High
Detects any HTTP request hitting the vulnerable Goobi viewer `/api/v[12]/index/stream` REST endpoint. The endpoint was removed in fix commit 326980f24c — on patched hosts this path should never appear in access logs; on unpatched hosts it should never be reachable from the public internet per the vendor's Apache/Tomcat block-list workaround. Any hit is therefore either a missed-patch indicator or active exploitation. Rationale: Endpoint path `/api/v[12]/index/stream` is the exact regex from the advisory's Apache httpd workaround block — no false-positive surface outside Goobi viewer. The fix removes the endpoint entirely, so any 2xx/3xx response is detection-grade. CIM Web datamodel + W3CIISLog + Sigma `webserver` category give cross-stack coverage; Defender XDR has no native HTTP request-path schema and is therefore omitted. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2rgp-f66f-4499 • https://solr.apache.org/guide/solr/latest/query-guide/streaming-expressions.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1212
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Goobi viewer CVE-2026-45083 — any access to the removed Solr streaming proxy
let GoobiEndpointRegex = @"(?i)/api/v[12]/index/stream";
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem matches regex GoobiEndpointRegex
| where csMethod in~ ("POST","GET")
| where scStatus !startswith "4" and scStatus !startswith "5"   // exclude denied/error
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csUserName,
          csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus, TimeTaken
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Destructive Solr streaming expression (update/delete/commit) via Goobi viewer proxy Actions on Objectives High
Higher-fidelity follow-on to the endpoint-access detection — surfaces requests whose query string or body carries a destructive Solr streaming-expression function (`delete(`, `update(`, `commit(`). The advisory explicitly calls these out as enabling permanent index modification or full-collection deletion. Reads (`search(`) are intentionally excluded to keep the signal tight to integrity-impact exploitation. Rationale: Solr streaming expressions documented at solr.apache.org name `delete()`, `update()`, `commit()` as the integrity-impacting functions; the advisory explicitly cites `update()` and `delete()` as enabling field overwrite and full-collection deletion. Combining the article's exact endpoint regex with these function names yields near-zero FP surface — there is no legitimate caller of this endpoint after the patch (it was removed). URL-encoded `%28` variants are included to defeat trivial obfuscation. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2rgp-f66f-4499 • https://solr.apache.org/guide/solr/latest/query-guide/streaming-expressions.html

W3CIISLog

| where csUriQuery has_any (DestructiveFunctions)
   or csUriQuery has "delete%28" or csUriQuery has "update%28" or csUriQuery has "commit%28"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csUserName,
          csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus, TimeTaken
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Obot /mcp-connect/{id} authenticated-user fan-out (ACR bypass probing) Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the GHSA-vw82-7fv8-r6gp exploit pattern: a single authenticated Obot user hits 5+ distinct MCP server IDs via POST /mcp-connect/{id} inside 10 minutes. Legitimate users interact with 1-2 MCP servers; rapid enumeration across many IDs is the post-bypass discovery shape called out in the advisory's reproduction steps. Rationale: Built around the exact exploit primitive in the advisory's reproduction section — POST /mcp-connect/<mcp_server_id> with an authenticated session. Fan-out threshold (5 distinct IDs / 10m) reflects the attacker workflow of probing which IDs are reachable post-bypass; benign users discover MCP servers via the (correctly-gated) connector picker and stick to 1-2. Cross-checked GitHub advisory GHSA-vw82-7fv8-r6gp; no public second-source PoCs surfaced. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vw82-7fv8-r6gp
ATT&CKT1190 T1078 T1213
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Obot ACR bypass — same user POSTing /mcp-connect/<id> against many distinct MCP server IDs in 10m
// Requires reverse proxy fronting Obot to be IIS-logging to Sentinel (W3CIISLog). For nginx/ALB/traefik
// use CommonSecurityLog / Syslog with the same regex on the URL path.
let WindowMin = 10m;
let FanoutThreshold = 5;     // empirical — legit users interact with 1-2 MCP servers
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where csMethod =~ "POST"
| where scStatus == 200
| where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)^/mcp-connect/[^/]+/?$"
| extend McpServerId = extract(@"(?i)^/mcp-connect/([^/?]+)", 1, csUriStem)
| where isnotempty(McpServerId)
| where isnotempty(csUserName)                 // authenticated only — anonymous would be 401
| summarize DistinctMcpIds = dcount(McpServerId),
            McpIdSet      = make_set(McpServerId, 50),
            HitCount      = count(),
            FirstSeen     = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen      = max(TimeGenerated),
            SrcIPs        = make_set(cIP, 10),
            UA            = any(csUserAgent)
            by csUserName, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where DistinctMcpIds >= FanoutThreshold
| project TimeGenerated, csUserName, DistinctMcpIds, McpIdSet, HitCount, FirstSeen, LastSeen, SrcIPs, UA
| order by DistinctMcpIds desc, LastSeen desc

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rex field=SampledUrls "/mcp-connect/(?<McpId>[^/?\s\"]+)"
| where DistinctMcpIds>=5 AND user!=""
| sort - DistinctMcpIds

[LLM] First-time-seen authenticated user → MCP server ID pairing on /mcp-connect Actions on Objectives Medium
Anti-baseline hunt for GHSA-vw82-7fv8-r6gp: surface a successful POST to /mcp-connect/<id> where the (user, mcp_server_id) pair has never been observed in the prior 30 days. Direct expression of the advisory's threat model — Basic Users reaching MCP servers they were never a member of any granting registry for. Rationale: Anti-baseline expression of the advisory's exact harm: a Basic User reaching an MCP server they were never a member of any granting MCP Registry for. The (csUserName, McpServerId) leftanti join surfaces novel pairings — the inverse of the legitimate intended flow described in the advisory's 'Vulnerability Details' section. Cross-checked against GHSA-vw82-7fv8-r6gp; affected version <= v0.21.0. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vw82-7fv8-r6gp

Data sourcesWeb.Web
// First-time-seen Obot user → MCP server ID pair (anti-baseline against 30 days)
// Use this as a hunt; promote to alerting once baseline maturity is confirmed (>= 21 days of W3CIISLog retention).
let Lookback   = 30d;
let RecentWin  = 4h;
let ExtractMcpId = (s:string) { extract(@"(?i)^/mcp-connect/([^/?]+)", 1, s) };
let Baseline =
    W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(Lookback) .. ago(RecentWin))
    | where csMethod =~ "POST" and scStatus == 200
    | where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)^/mcp-connect/[^/]+/?$"
    | extend McpServerId = ExtractMcpId(csUriStem)
    | where isnotempty(csUserName) and isnotempty(McpServerId)
    | summarize by csUserName, McpServerId;
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(RecentWin)
| where csMethod =~ "POST" and scStatus == 200
| where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)^/mcp-connect/[^/]+/?$"
| extend McpServerId = ExtractMcpId(csUriStem)
| where isnotempty(csUserName) and isnotempty(McpServerId)
| join kind=leftanti Baseline on csUserName, McpServerId
| summarize FirstHit  = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastHit   = max(TimeGenerated),
            HitCount  = count(),
            SrcIPs    = make_set(cIP, 10),
            UA        = any(csUserAgent)
            by csUserName, McpServerId
| order by FirstHit desc
source:nginx @http.method:POST @http.status_code:200 @http.url_details.path:*/mcp-connect/*
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t min(_time) as FirstSeen, count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url="*/mcp-connect/*" Web.http_method=POST Web.status=200 earliest=-30d@d latest=-4h by Web.user, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rex field=url "/mcp-connect/(?<McpId>[^/?\s\"]+)"
| fields user, McpId
| inputlookup append=t obot_mcp_access_recent.csv
| eval pair=user."|".McpId
| stats count, values(*) as * by pair
| where count==1   // pair only in recent window, not in 30d baseline
| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as FirstSeen, count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url="*/mcp-connect/*" Web.http_method=POST Web.status=200 earliest=-30d@d latest=-4h by Web.user, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'

level: high

[LLM] Mapfish Print Servlet running on host — CVE-2026-44672 exposure hunt Reconnaissance High
Identifies hosts where a Java process is running the Mapfish Print servlet (org.mapfish.print:print-lib / print-servlet) by anchoring on the Maven coordinates in the JVM command line. Use the output to enumerate exposure to CVE-2026-44672 (unauthenticated RCE in the Dynamic table feature) and reconcile installed version against patched matrix: >=3.23.0<3.28.28, >=3.29.0<3.30.30, >=3.31.0<3.31.21, >=3.32.0<3.33.14, >=3.34.0<4.0.3. Rationale: Article gives Maven coordinates org.mapfish.print:print-lib and org.mapfish.print:print-servlet plus the precise vulnerable version matrix. Anchoring on those strings inside java cmdline is high-fidelity (no other product uses these coords) and the regex extracts the running version so analysts can reconcile against the patched matrix in one pass. Cross-checked against the GHSA itself plus the Mapfish Print servlet source (MapPrinterServlet.java) and Jasper template injection background. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q7m6-wpvf-mvwx • https://github.com/mapfish/mapfish-print/blob/master/core/src/main/java/org/mapfish/print/servlet/MapPrinterServlet.java • https://insinuator.net/2023/06/jasper-reports-library-code-injection/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("java.exe","javaw.exe","java")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("mapfish-print","print-servlet","org.mapfish.print")
| extend MapfishVersion = extract(@"(?:print-lib|print-servlet|mapfish-print)-(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| extend Cve = "CVE-2026-44672",
         Note = "Vulnerable if 3.23.0-3.28.27, 3.29.0-3.30.29, 3.31.0-3.31.20, 3.32.0-3.33.13, 3.34.0-4.0.2"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine), Versions = make_set(MapfishVersion, 10)
            by DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, Cve, Note
| order by LastSeen desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("java.exe","javaw.exe","java")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("mapfish-print","print-servlet","org.mapfish.print")
| extend MapfishVersion = extract(@"(?:print-lib|print-servlet|mapfish-print)-(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, TargetProcessCommandLine)
| extend Cve = "CVE-2026-44672"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            SampleCmd = any(TargetProcessCommandLine), Versions = make_set(MapfishVersion, 10)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, Cve
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] OS shell or LOLBin spawned by Java process hosting Mapfish Print (CVE-2026-44672 exploit) Exploitation High
Hunts for command shells, scripting hosts, or recon LOLBins spawned as children of a java/javaw process whose own command line references the Mapfish Print servlet. Successful exploitation of CVE-2026-44672 (Jasper template injection in the Dynamic table feature) materialises as the JVM invoking Runtime.exec on attacker-supplied commands — visible here as java→cmd/powershell/bash/curl/whoami/etc. Rationale: The article specifies the exact Maven artifact (org.mapfish.print:print-lib / print-servlet) but no exploit-payload strings. The high-fidelity signal therefore comes from pairing (a) parent-process anchor = java/javaw whose cmdline contains the Mapfish Print coordinates with (b) child-process anchor = OS shells/LOLBins. java spawning a shell is anomalous for a Spring/Tomcat-hosted Mapfish Print process under normal operation and is the canonical post-exploitation footprint of Jasper template injection (Runtime.getRuntime().exec). Cross-checked against the Mapfish Print upstream servlet code and the Insinuator write-up on Jasper Reports template injection (same vuln class). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q7m6-wpvf-mvwx • https://github.com/mapfish/mapfish-print/blob/master/core/src/main/java/org/mapfish/print/servlet/MapPrinterServlet.java • https://insinuator.net/2023/06/jasper-reports-library-code-injection/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059 T1059.001 T1059.003 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe","javaw.exe","java")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("mapfish-print","print-servlet","org.mapfish.print")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","nslookup.exe","wmic.exe","sh","bash","dash","ksh","busybox","id","uname","hostname")
| extend Cve = "CVE-2026-44672", Family = "Mapfish Print Jasper-template RCE"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, Cve, Family
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("java.exe","javaw.exe","java")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("mapfish-print","print-servlet","org.mapfish.print")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","nslookup.exe","wmic.exe","/bin/sh","/bin/bash","/bin/dash","/usr/bin/sh","/usr/bin/bash","busybox","/usr/bin/id","/usr/bin/uname","/usr/bin/hostname")
| extend Cve = "CVE-2026-44672"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, Cve
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] SillyTavern CVE-2026-44650 unauthenticated POST to vulnerable /api/extensions/* endpoints Exploitation High
Detects POST requests to the five SillyTavern endpoints vulnerable to path-traversal-via-dot ('.') wipe of the user extensions directory: /api/extensions/{delete,update,version,branches,switch}. Targets the network/web-log pivot — the exploit is a single POST that returns HTTP 200 with a body referencing 'data\default-user\extensions'. Because no auth is required in default config (basicAuthMode:false), any source IP reaching the listener is suspect. Rationale: Article-specific URI stems are verbatim from the GHSA PoC (`POST /api/extensions/delete` with body `{"extensionName":"."}`) and the explicit 'Same Pattern in Other Endpoints' list (`/update`, `/version`, `/branches`, `/switch`). No auth means a single 200-OK POST to any of these paths is exploitation. Cross-checked against the DailyCVE write-up which confirms the same five endpoints and PoC shape. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-886q-f44j-h6wh • https://dailycve.com/sillytavern-unauthenticated-path-traversal-directory-deletion-cve-n-a-critical/ • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pkg/npm/sillytavern/CVE-2026-34524/
ATT&CKT1190 T1485
Data sourcesWeb
// Defender XDR has no native HTTP-server access-log table; this falls back to the egress pivot: a host that *initiated* a POST to a SillyTavern listener.
// Most useful where Defender-managed clients (browsers / curl from compromised hosts) hit the vulnerable instance.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/api/extensions/delete","/api/extensions/update","/api/extensions/version","/api/extensions/branches","/api/extensions/switch")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","curl.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","python.exe","node.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
// Covers IIS-fronted, App-Service-fronted, CEF/firewall, and any ASIM-normalised web telemetry feeding the SillyTavern listener.
let vulnPaths = dynamic(["/api/extensions/delete","/api/extensions/update","/api/extensions/version","/api/extensions/branches","/api/extensions/switch"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csMethod =~ "POST"
  | where csUriStem has_any (vulnPaths)
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=cIP, DstHost=Computer, Method=csMethod, Uri=csUriStem, Status=scStatus, UserAgent=csUserAgent, Source="W3CIISLog"),
(AppServiceHTTPLogs
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where CsMethod =~ "POST"
  | where CsUriStem has_any (vulnPaths)
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=CIp, DstHost=CsHost, Method=CsMethod, Uri=CsUriStem, Status=ScStatus, UserAgent=UserAgent, Source="AppServiceHTTPLogs"),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
  | where RequestURL has_any (vulnPaths)
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=SourceIP, DstHost=DestinationHostName, Method=RequestMethod, Uri=RequestURL, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, Source="CommonSecurityLog"),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where HttpMethod =~ "POST"

  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, DstHost=DstHostname, Method=HttpMethod, Uri=Url, Status=tostring(HttpStatusCode), UserAgent=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, Source="ImWebSession")
| where Status startswith "2" or Status == "200"
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] node.exe bulk-deletes SillyTavern data\*\extensions\ directory (CVE-2026-44650 post-exploit) Actions on Objectives High
Detects the destructive side-effect of CVE-2026-44650: the SillyTavern node.exe process recursively deleting files under `data\<user>\extensions\`. The GHSA PoC shows `fs.promises.rm(extensionPath, { recursive: true })` against `data\default-user\extensions` — this surfaces as a tight burst of FileDeleted events from a single node.exe PID against files under that path. Hits even when no web logs are retained. Rationale: PoC body 'Extension has been deleted at data\default-user\extensions' confirms the destructive path pattern — `<basePath>\data\<user>\extensions\`. SillyTavern is a Node app so the deleting process is `node.exe`. Threshold of 5 deletions/minute distinguishes a wipe from the single-file legitimate uninstall (which removes one extension subdir, typically 1-3 files in one event). Cross-checked against related SillyTavern path-traversal CVEs (2026-34522/-34523/-34524) which describe the same parent directory layout. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-886q-f44j-h6wh • https://dailycve.com/sillytavern-unauthenticated-path-traversal-directory-deletion-cve-n-a-critical/ • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pkg/npm/sillytavern/CVE-2026-34524/

| summarize DeletedCount = count(),
            FirstDeletion = min(TimeGenerated),

            SamplePaths   = make_set(TargetFilePath, 10)
            by DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)

| order by FirstDeletion desc

[LLM] esm.sh CVE-2026-44593 legacy router path-traversal exploitation in web logs Exploitation High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests targeting an esm.sh deployment that combine URL-encoded path traversal (`..%2f` / `%2e%2e%2f`) with the URL-encoded fragment-bypass (`%23%2f..`) used to coerce the legacy router into writing arbitrary files via `buildStorage.Put`. The double-pattern (traversal AND fragment) is the exact signature of the PoC and is extremely unusual in normal traffic. Rationale: Built on the exact URL pattern in the GHSA PoC: every exploit URL must combine URL-encoded `../` segments (`..%2f`/`%2e%2e%2f`) with the URL-encoded fragment (`%23`) followed by more `..%2f` — that's how the path normaliser walks out of `legacy/v.../esnext/...` to `/tmp/pwned`. Either pattern alone has plausible legitimate uses (crawlers, raw fragment URIs); the combination on a single request is the exploit signature. Did not search the web — article is self-contained with a complete PoC and authoritative GHSA reference.
ATT&CKT1190 T1083 T1505.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Defender XDR has no native inbound-HTTP-server table; this is best-effort
// against outbound HTTP visibility on Defender-monitored clients that may be
// internal red-teamers or attackers probing the org-hosted esm.sh.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("HttpConnectionInspected","ConnectionSuccess")
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("..%2f","..%2F","%2e%2e%2f","%2e%2e%2F")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("%23%2f..","%23%2F..","%23/..")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
let traversal = dynamic(["..%2f","..%2F","%2e%2e%2f","%2e%2e%2F"]);
let fragBypass = dynamic(["%23%2f..","%23%2F..","%23/.."]);
union isfuzzy=true
  ( W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | extend FullUri = strcat(csUriStem, iff(isempty(csUriQuery), "", strcat("?", csUriQuery)))
    | where FullUri has_any (traversal) and FullUri has_any (fragBypass)
    | project TimeGenerated, Src=cIP, Host=Computer, Site=sSiteName, Uri=FullUri, Method=csMethod, Status=scStatus, UA=csUserAgent, _Source="IIS"),
  ( CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where isnotempty(RequestURL)
    | where RequestURL has_any (traversal) and RequestURL has_any (fragBypass)
    | project TimeGenerated, Src=SourceIP, Host=DestinationHostName, Site=DeviceProduct, Uri=RequestURL, Method=RequestMethod, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), UA=RequestClientApplication, _Source="CEF"),
  ( ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where isnotempty(Url)
    | where Url has_any (traversal) and Url has_any (fragBypass)
    | project TimeGenerated, Src=SrcIpAddr, Host=DstHostname, Site=EventProduct, Uri=Url, Method=HttpMethod, Status=tostring(HttpStatusCode), UA=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, _Source="ASIM")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: esm.sh Legacy Router Path Traversal Exploitation (CVE-2026-44593)
id: 4a3d8b1c-5f2e-4b8a-9c3d-1e7f6a2b8c9d
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects inbound HTTP requests that combine URL-encoded path traversal sequences
  with the URL-encoded fragment-bypass pattern used to exploit CVE-2026-44593 in
  esm.sh. The vulnerable legacy router concatenates path components without
  sanitisation, allowing the %23 (#) fragment plus repeated ..%2f segments to
  normalise the storage key to arbitrary filesystem locations on the server.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3636-h3vx-6465
  - https://github.com/esm-dev/esm.sh/blob/4312ae93e518121e764a18bb521af12e490ef137/server/legacy_router.go#L291

logsource:

detection:

      - '..%2f'
      - '..%2F'
      - '%2e%2e%2f'
      - '%2e%2e%2F'
  selection_fragment_bypass:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '%23%2f..'
      - '%23%2F..'
      - '%23/..'
  condition: selection_traversal and selection_fragment_bypass
fields:
  - c-ip

  - cs-uri-query
  - cs-user-agent
  - sc-status
falsepositives:
  - Internal vulnerability scanners (Qualys, Nessus, Nuclei) testing for path traversal — allowlist scanner source IPs
  - Security researchers exercising the PoC against a non-production esm.sh instance
level: high

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| eval esmsh_route=if(match(url, "(?i)/v\d+/|/legacy/|/gh/"), "yes", "no")

[LLM] esm.sh server writes file outside legacy storage path (CVE-2026-44593 post-exploit artefact) Installation High
Hunts file writes performed by the esm.sh server binary (or its child processes) to sensitive Linux paths outside the legitimate storage directory — the visible artefact of the arbitrary-file-write exploit chain that leads to RCE via overwritten binaries / cron / SSH authorized_keys. Pairs with UC1 to catch successful exploitation after the inbound request lands. Rationale: The article's mechanism is `buildStorage.Put` writing a normalised key like `/tmp/pwned` — i.e. ANY file landing on the host originated from the esm.sh process. Pinning to `InitiatingProcessFileName has 'esm.sh'` and then anti-allowlisting the legitimate storage directory turns this into a deployment-aware alert that fires on the post-exploit artefact. PoC explicitly writes to `/tmp/pwned`; real attackers will pivot to `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys`, cron, or `/usr/local/bin/` for RCE — all covered. Did not search the web — the GHSA advisory is the canonical source and the exploit chain is unambiguous.
ATT&CKT1190 T1574 T1098.004 T1053.003

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "esm.sh"
    or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "esm.sh"
    or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "esm-dev"
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "esm.sh"
| where not(FolderPath has_any (_esmsh_storage))
| where FolderPath has_any (_sensitive_prefixes) or FileName endswith "authorized_keys" or FolderPath has ".ssh/"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,

| order by Timestamp desc

title: esm.sh Server Writes Outside Storage Path (CVE-2026-44593 Post-Exploit)
id: 7c2e9a4b-8d1f-4e5b-9a7c-3f2d8e1b4c5a
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects the esm.sh Go server (vulnerable to CVE-2026-44593) writing files to
  sensitive Linux paths outside its legitimate storage directory. The legacy
  router path-traversal lets an attacker direct buildStorage.Put to overwrite
  arbitrary files; flagging writes to /tmp, /etc, /usr/{,local}/bin, /root,
  cron locations, or any .ssh/ directory catches the resulting filesystem
  artefact regardless of which URL pattern smuggled the traversal.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3636-h3vx-6465
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/13
tags:
  - attack.initial-access
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1098.004
  - attack.t1053.003
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|contains:
      - 'esm.sh'
      - 'esm-dev'
  selection_target:
    TargetFilename|startswith:
      - '/tmp/'
      - '/etc/'
      - '/usr/bin/'
      - '/usr/sbin/'
      - '/usr/local/bin/'
      - '/root/'
      - '/var/spool/cron/'
      - '/etc/cron.'
      - '/opt/'
  selection_ssh:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/.ssh/authorized_keys'
      - '/.ssh/id_'
  filter_storage:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/var/lib/esm'
      - '/var/cache/esm'
      - '/data/esm'
      - '/srv/esm'
      - '/opt/esm/storage'
      - '/cache/'
      - '/storage/'
  condition: selection_proc and (selection_target or selection_ssh) and not filter_storage
fields:
  - Image

  - User

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate operator restarting esm.sh and writing logs to /tmp or /opt — allowlist the deployment's actual storage path in filter_storage
level: high
source:linux.auditd @process.name:(*esm.sh* OR *esm-dev*) (@file.path:/tmp/* OR @file.path:/etc/* OR @file.path:/usr/bin/* OR @file.path:/usr/local/bin/* OR @file.path:/usr/sbin/* OR @file.path:/root/* OR @file.path:/var/spool/cron/* OR @file.path:/etc/cron.* OR @file.path:*/.ssh/authorized_keys OR @file.path:*/.ssh/id_*) -@file.path:*/storage/* -@file.path:*/cache/* -@file.path:/var/lib/esm/* -@file.path:/data/esm/*

[LLM] Affected hosts running vulnerable Azure Key Vault Keys Java SDK (CVE-2026-33117) Exploitation High
Surfaces every device whose Defender TVM inventory shows the maven coordinate com.azure:azure-security-keyvault-keys at a version below 4.10.6. Article-specific because it pivots on the exact CVE ID and package, not generic 'unpatched Java library'. Rationale: Pivots on the exact CVE ID and maven package coordinate from the advisory; TVM inventory is authoritative for installed components. Cross-checked NVD entry and MSRC advisory linked from the GHSA; CVSS 9.1, fixed in 4.10.6 confirmed. [LLM] Vulnerable azure-security-keyvault-keys JAR (<4.10.6) written to disk Installation Medium
Catches the vulnerable Maven artifact landing on disk via build pipeline, application deployment, or developer fetch — covers cases where TVM hasn't yet inventoried the host (new deploy, shaded build extracted). Version comparison is done via parse_version against the fixed release 4.10.6. Rationale: Maven artifact filename convention is deterministic — every vulnerable copy of the SDK on disk will match azure-security-keyvault-keys-<X.Y.Z>.jar with X.Y.Z < 4.10.6, the version range the advisory explicitly calls out. Catches gaps where TVM doesn't yet see the host. Cross-checked the fix commit 1b5c5c7 in the azure-sdk-for-java repo to confirm 4.10.6 as the fixed version. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-97jf-46m3-8953 • https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-java/commit/1b5c5c79d85a5c9a9cfd07f6cdff6fd0f50eccf9 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-33117

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFileName, Version, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername, TargetFileSHA256

title: Vulnerable Azure Key Vault Keys Java SDK JAR Written (CVE-2026-33117)
id: 8b1f3d5a-9c4e-4f6b-a2d1-7e0c4b9f8a12
status: experimental
description: Detects the on-disk presence of azure-security-keyvault-keys Java SDK JAR at a version below the fixed 4.10.6, indicating an application or build pipeline pulling in the vulnerable cryptographic-verification path.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-97jf-46m3-8953

  condition: selection_vuln
falsepositives:
  - Developer ~/.m2/repository or Gradle cache containing historical versions

| Minor := splitString(Version, by="\\.", index=1)
| Patch := splitString(Version, by="\\.", index=2)
| Major := number(Major) | Minor := number(Minor) | Patch := number(Patch)

TeamPCP's Mini Shai-Hulud Is Back: A Self-Spreading Supply Chain Attack Compromises TanStack npm Packages

StepSecurity
2026-05-12 14 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The Mini Shai-Hulud worm is actively compromising legitimate npm packages by hijacking CI/CD pipelines and stealing developer secrets. StepSecurity's OSS Package Security Feed first detected the attack in official @tanstack packages and is tracking its spread across the ecosystem in real time.

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud npm Worm C2 callback to Session Protocol CDN and masscan.cloud Command & Control High
Detects DNS resolution or outbound TCP/UDP to the Session Protocol seed nodes (seed1.getsession.org, filev2.getsession.org) and api.masscan.cloud used by TeamPCP's Mini Shai-Hulud worm to exfiltrate harvested CI/CD secrets and developer credentials. These hostnames are not part of any legitimate enterprise software supply chain and any contact is high-fidelity. Rationale: Domains seed1.getsession.org, filev2.getsession.org, and api.masscan.cloud are named explicitly as the worm's exfiltration channel in the StepSecurity write-up. Session Protocol nodes have zero legitimate enterprise use and api.masscan.cloud is the same C2 infrastructure observed across the @antv variant (memory observation 1252) — high-fidelity primary IOCs across multiple StepSecurity / Socket.dev / JFrog reports on the campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1567/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1567 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
let CampaignHosts = dynamic(["seed1.getsession.org","filev2.getsession.org","api.masscan.cloud"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where RemoteUrl has_any (CampaignHosts) or tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host) in~ (CampaignHosts)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountUpn=InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, Indicator=coalesce(RemoteUrl, RemoteIP), Source="network", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName;
let EvHits = DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType in ("DnsQueryResponse","ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionFailed","NetworkConnectionEvents")
  | where RemoteUrl has_any (CampaignHosts) or AdditionalFields has_any (CampaignHosts)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountUpn=InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, Indicator=coalesce(RemoteUrl, tostring(AdditionalFields)), Source="device-event", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName=tostring(parse_json(""));
NetHits
| union EvHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let CampaignHosts = dynamic(["seed1.getsession.org","filev2.getsession.org","api.masscan.cloud"]);
let DnsHits = DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name has_any (CampaignHosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Indicator=Name, Source="DnsEvents";
let AsimDns = ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (CampaignHosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Indicator=DnsQuery, Source="ImDnsActivity";
let ProxyHits = CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationHostName has_any (CampaignHosts) or RequestURL has_any (CampaignHosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Indicator=coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), Source="Proxy/CEF";
let WebHits = ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where HttpHostName has_any (CampaignHosts) or Url has_any (CampaignHosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Indicator=coalesce(HttpHostName, Url), Source="ImWebSession";
DnsHits | union AsimDns, ProxyHits, WebHits
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Hits=count() by Computer, ClientIP, Indicator, Source
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] TeamPCP Mini Shai-Hulud stealer payload hash match (SHA256/SHA1) Installation High
Alerts on disk-write or in-memory execution of a binary whose SHA256 or SHA1 matches the obfuscated 2.3 MB credential-stealer payload published by TeamPCP across @tanstack, @uipath, @draftlab and other compromised npm packages. The hashes are the cleanest single-source-of-truth IOCs in this campaign and are reused unchanged across all 50+ compromised package versions. Rationale: Four SHA256 and three SHA1 hashes were published in the StepSecurity article as the canonical fingerprint of the 2.3 MB obfuscated stealer payload. These hashes were observed unchanged across all listed @tanstack/@uipath/@draftlab versions and were corroborated in earlier @antv variant reporting (Socket.dev, JFrog, StepSecurity — memory observations 1249, 1250, 1252). Hash-based hunting carries zero ambiguity and zero FP risk against benign software. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1027

  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, Source="DeviceProcessEvents";
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents

  | where SHA256 in~ (StealerSha256) or SHA1 in~ (StealerSha1)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, Source="DeviceFileEvents";
let ImgHits = DeviceImageLoadEvents
